alert.raw: MEDIUM: PowerShell.exe executed with -EncodedCommand flag by service account svc_deploy. Process spawned from Windows service. WMI queries and registry modifications observed on domain controller.

telemetry.detail: svchost.exe (SCCM client service, PID 1440) launched powershell.exe -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -NonInteractive -encodedcommand [482-char base64 payload]

telemetry.event: Script path resolved from encoded payload
telemetry.detail: Decoded: & 'C:\Program Files\Microsoft Configuration Manager\Bin\Deploy.ps1' — file present, expected installation path
Deploy.ps1: Authenticode signature valid. Publisher: Microsoft Corporation. Certificate chain: DigiCert → Microsoft Code Signing PCA → Microsoft Corporation. Not expired (exp: 2027-03-15).
SELECT * FROM Win32_Product WHERE InstallDate > '20260601' — standard SCCM software inventory scan, no anomalous fields
HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\SMS\Mobile Client\Compliance\LastScanTime set to 2026-06-28T14:22:45Z — SCCM compliance namespace, expected artifact
powershell.exe exited with code 0. No child processes spawned. No network connections initiated. No files written outside SCCM paths.

cachedVerdict.reasoning: This alert is a well-understood false positive from the encoded-PowerShell heuristic rule (PS-EncodedCmd) firing on legitimate Microsoft SCCM (System Center Configuration Manager) activity. Every indicator points unambiguously to benign deployment operations: the parent process is the known SCCM client service (svchost.exe, PID 1440), the decoded script resides at the expected Microsoft Configuration Manager installation path, the script carries a valid Authenticode signature from Microsoft Corporation with an unbroken certificate chain, WMI queries match SCCM software inventory patterns seen every patch cycle, and the only registry write is to the Microsoft SMS compliance namespace. The service account svc_deploy is the expected SCCM service account. No network connections, no child processes, no persistence — textbook clean execution.

timeline.significance: Expected parent process — SCCM routinely uses encoded PowerShell for deployment automation
Known-good path under Microsoft Configuration Manager; no obfuscation after decoding
Valid code-signing chain — script cannot have been tampered with post-signing
Routine compliance check consistent with monthly patch-Tuesday cadence
Expected operational side-effect; confined entirely to Microsoft SMS namespace
No persistence, no network, no child processes — clean execution lifecycle

evidence.signal: Parent process: SCCM client service (svchost.exe, PID 1440)
evidence.why_it_matters: Legitimate orchestration context — not spawned from Office, browser, or user interaction

evidence.signal: Microsoft Authenticode signature valid with full certificate chain
evidence.why_it_matters: Cryptographic guarantee the script has not been modified since Microsoft signed it
No run keys, no startup folders, no scheduled tasks — zero persistence indicators

evidence.signal: Zero network connections, zero child processes on exit
evidence.why_it_matters: A malicious script would typically beacon out, download a stage 2, or spawn cmd.exe — none of that occurred

containment.target: CORP-SRV-DC01 — activity is fully explained by SCCM operations
containment.rationale: This is a false positive; any containment action would disrupt legitimate patch management

containment.action: Tune encoded-PowerShell detection rule to exclude SCCM client parent process
containment.target: EDR rule: PS-EncodedCmd — add exclusion for svchost.exe parenting to known SCCM paths
containment.rationale: Reduce noise during patch windows; maintain coverage for non-SCCM encoded-command usage

cachedVerdict.ciso_summary: Our automated security system triggered a false alarm when the IT team ran a scheduled software update — the activity was a legitimate, Microsoft-signed maintenance script running on our domain controller. No attack occurred, no data was accessed inappropriately, and no systems were compromised. We are fine-tuning our detection settings to prevent similar false alarms during routine IT maintenance windows.
cachedVerdict.summary: False positive: legitimate Microsoft SCCM deployment script triggered the encoded-PowerShell rule. Signed Microsoft tooling, expected SCCM service account, benign WMI + registry activity only. No action required.
